findings.title: next 16.3.1 — three unauthenticated RCE advisories (Windows dev server, Image Optimization API/AVIF, next/og ImageResponse)
findings.entry_point: HTTP (self-hosted next start / _next/image / og image routes)
findings.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments (image optimization endpoint and og image generation are network-reachable; Windows-hosted dev/start servers directly exploitable).
findings.remediation: npm install next@16.3.8 eslint-config-next@16.3.8 (patch within major 16, non-semver-major per npm audit).

findings.title: deepmerge-ts <8.0.0 — stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs (via prisma / @prisma/config)
findings.entry_point: prisma CLI / prisma.config.ts loading (install + build lifecycle)
findings.impact: Process crash/DoS of the Prisma CLI when merging attacker-influenced recursive config graphs. Build-time surface, not on the HTTP runtime path of this app.
findings.remediation: package.json overrides: deepmerge-ts ^8.0.2 (avoided npm-audit --force downgrade of prisma 7 -> 6 which would break the schema/config setup).

findings.title: mysql2 <=3.23.0 — auth plugin downgrade leaks plaintext credentials + zlib decompression bomb DoS (via prisma)
findings.entry_point: prisma engines/CLI (MySQL path). NOTE: this app uses @prisma/adapter-pg (PostgreSQL); mysql2 is transitive and not imported by application code
findings.impact: Credential leak on downgrade attack and memory DoS on compressed MySQL protocol traffic — reachable only where a MySQL connection is made (not this app's runtime path).

findings.title: brace-expansion — quadratic-time expansion + uncontrolled recursion DoS (transitive)
findings.impact: Stack exhaustion / CPU DoS on crafted brace patterns; tooling surface.

findings.title: fast-uri 3.0.0-3.1.7 — host confusion / SSRF family via malformed URI normalization (transitive)
findings.impact: Incorrect URI canonicalization can produce host confusion / SSRF in consumers of fast-uri.

findings.title: js-yaml 4.0.0-4.3.1 — maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources (transitive)
findings.impact: CPU exhaustion on crafted YAML merge sources; tooling surface.

findings.title: sharp <0.35.4 — libheif vulnerabilities (double free / memory safety) in image decode path
findings.entry_point: next image optimization (sharp used server-side to process uploaded/remote images)
findings.impact: Memory corruption / DoS when image optimization decodes a crafted HEIF-family image via the network-reachable image endpoint (self-hosted).
